sessions.goal: Play the first 15 minutes as a brand-new player who has never seen the game; note every moment of confusion.
sessions.verdict: The Survey step is an excellent onboarding: every checklist line teaches what to look at, and the roof-hole hint ('stand under it, look up') worked first try. Clear is satisfying when feedback is visible (the snow shovelling, sawing the rafter into three carryable lengths), but it drags. It takes 15 single-item trips to the door, and sweeping happens in a near-dark room where you cannot see what is dirty. After 14 game minutes I was still in step 2 of 5. Lighting and readability during Clear matter most.

sessions.goal: Finish the Survey and the whole Clear step (haul the debris, saw the fallen rafter, shovel the snow, sweep the floor, scrub the walls and the chimney) using only what the screen tells you; record the game time each checklist line completes. Say whether sawing keeps its progress when you let go of the button, whether the debris counter ever goes up, and whether you can see which parts of the floor and walls are still dirty.
sessions.verdict: Survey, hauling, sawing, snow and chimney all read well from the screen: sawing keeps its progress when you let go (6% -> 12% across a release), the floor and chimney visibly brighten where cleaned, and status lines explain everything including why the debris count rises from 15 to 17. The Clear step falls down on its last two lines: the walls scrub at ~4% per 25 s with almost no visible clean/grimy difference, and the floor's last 7% hides in dim corners, so the step could not be finished in 28 minutes of play.

sessions.goal: Your save (written by the previous release, 0.1.2) starts at the Repair step with the cabin already cleared. First say whether the game loaded it without complaint. Then finish Repair and as much of Furnish as you can: pry up the rotten floorboards and lay new planks in every gap, shingle every open roof section, take down the window boards, mend the chair and table, then bring the furnishings in from the wagon, place them and turn them with R. Record the game time of each checklist line; say plainly whether every floor gap and every roof hole could be found, aimed at and fixed.
sessions.verdict: The 0.1.2 save loaded cleanly ('Loaded your save.') at Repair, and the whole Repair step works: all 3 rotten boards could be found (they show as dark/green patches), pried, re-planked, and all 4 roof sections shingled, with clear aim names, progress meters and warm status lines. The weak spots are the roof hole's visibility from below (the last open section was a sliver), the one-at-a-time board hauling, and R on wall furnishings: the sampler turned once with R hangs flat out of the wall but still counts.

sessions.goal: Your save starts early in the Kindle step: split firewood, stack it, lay and light the fire, welcome the settler and watch the reveal (do not skip it); then spend the rest of your time walking around inside and outside the cabin, judging how it looks and reads (the fire and the firelit chimney, the settler in her chair, the mare, labels and on-screen text overlapping, light and models) and noting anything ugly, broken, floating, clipping or hard to read.
sessions.verdict: The Kindle loop works end to end: split, stack, lay kindling and a log, strike and hold a match, and the cabin really does warm up, with lovely orange firelight on the stones and walls. The weak spots are aiming at small targets (the woodpile above all) and the payoff. Ada arrives and sits down off-screen in about 25 seconds before the reveal cuts in, she sits sideways in her chair, the player avatar blocks the fire in the final frame, and outside there is no chimney or smoke to show the cabin is lived in. Fixing the arrival and the closing shot would make the ending land.

findings.title: Framed sampler turned with R and hung on a log wall lies flat, sticking out of the wall edge-on
findings.detail: Took the framed sampler from the wagon, carried it in, pressed R once, faced the right-hand (+x) log wall at about 0.8 m and pressed E. It was hung, and the brief line 'Something of home on the walls' ticked, but the frame lies horizontal, perpendicular to the wall: from the front and from the side it shows only as a thin red/green line at eye height. Expected wall furnishings either to keep facing the room whatever R does, or to turn only about the wall's normal.
findings.repro: pt start --profile kindling --game-dir <kindling checkout> --seed 1 (save at Repair); finish Repair; at the wagon aim at 'Framed sampler', e; walk in through the door; face the +x wall (yaw 90) ~0.8 m away, pitch level; pt key r; pt key e; sidestep and look

findings.title: Scrub the walls is far slower than every other Clear task (13% -> 24% in ~70 s of continuous scrubbing)
findings.detail: With the scrub brush held against the log wall while sweeping the view across it, the walls line rose about 4% per 25 s of scrubbing (13% at tick 34455, 17% at 35363, 24% at 37966). Extrapolated, the walls alone need roughly 8-10 more minutes of holding the mouse, more than haul+snow+chimney together. Combined with the walls being hard to read (see below) it was the reason the Clear step could not be finished in a 35-minute session. Chimney, by comparison, went 0 -> 100% in ~1.5 min.
findings.repro: pt start --profile kindling --game-dir <kindling checkout> --seed 77; finish Survey; pt key 2; walk to any interior log wall until the meter shows '[---] 0% clean'; pt mousehold 25 while tapping arrow keys; watch 'Scrub the walls (N%)'

findings.title: A shingle lying on the snow drift takes the aim, so the shovel does nothing at the drift's edge
findings.detail: With the shovel out and the crosshair visibly on the snow drift's edge, holding the mouse for 4 s did nothing: the aim read 'Fallen shingle - Haul it out of the cabin.' Shovelling only started after the crosshair was nudged onto bare snow. That contradicts the stated rule that the shovel works anywhere on the drift's footprint. Once it started, the snow cleared in a few seconds, which felt good.
findings.repro: after Survey at about (0.8,0.4) yaw 297 pitch -45: key 3; mousehold 4 with the crosshair on the snow where a shingle overlaps it

findings.title: Ada arrives and settles out of sight, and the reveal cuts in before you can turn to see her
findings.detail: The fire took hold at tick 28337 ('Ada's wagon is coming up the trail'). 'Ada Lark is here' followed at 28491, she was already 'seated' by about 28780, and the REVEAL took over at 29100, about 25 game seconds in all. I was facing the fire, then the room. I saw her lines as subtitles ('This is home. Thank you.') but never saw her walk in or sit down before the reveal started. Nothing on screen prompts you to turn and greet her. Expected her arrival to be something you can watch (a prompt, a camera beat, or a wait for the player to look) before the reveal.
findings.repro: pt start; light the fire facing the hearth; pt face 180 as soon as 'Ada's wagon is coming' shows

findings.title: Ada sits turned sideways in the rocking chair, the armrest clipping through her
findings.detail: After Welcome, Ada Lark in the rocking chair by the hearth is rotated about 90 degrees from the chair. The quilted chair back is at her side rather than behind her, the near armrest runs through her lap and her skirt pokes out past the rockers (see also shots/ada7.png). Expected her to face the way the chair faces, with her back against the quilt.
findings.repro: pt start; finish Kindle and Welcome; from the hearth front, step right and pt face 60, tilt down a little

findings.title: Checklist and Ada's brief cover the upper-left third of the view, over the wagon bed and window
findings.detail: In Furnish the HUD has 8 lines. At the wagon the furnishings sit right under them, and at the window the top boards were under the checklist text. F1 hides only the controls help.
findings.repro: finish Repair; walkto wagon; look at the wagon bed

findings.title: Default help panel covers the lower third of the screen, where the floor and debris are
findings.detail: The controls help is shown at start and covers the bottom third of the view. That is exactly where the floor, debris and snow drift are when you tilt down to survey. A new player has to find F1 (mentioned only inside the panel) to see what they are aiming at. The help is clear and useful, but it could shrink or fade after the first minute.
findings.repro: pt start ...; walk in the door; hold Down 0.6

findings.title: E meant for a broken board on the floor silently set the table upright instead
findings.detail: While picking up the window boards (E, looking down near the window), one E press with no board under the crosshair righted the overturned table ('You set the table back on its legs.', tick 20127). Harmless here, but the 'Set the table right' line ticked without me choosing it; I only noticed later from the checklist. The status line says what happened, so it is workable.
findings.repro: after prying off the window boards, stand near the window and press e at the floor between the boards and the table

findings.title: E next to the Fallen rafter says 'Nothing to pick up there' instead of saying it must be sawn
findings.detail: Standing 0.7 m from the Fallen rafter (the nearest debris) and pressing E shows 'Nothing to pick up there.' The 'Too long to carry. Saw it (4)' hint only shows when the crosshair is exactly on the rafter. While hauling debris I thought the game was ignoring me. Once the rafter was sawn, the feedback was excellent ('Sawn into three lengths...').
findings.repro: after Survey: walkto debris until it picks the Fallen rafter; key e

findings.title: Fallen rafter needs an exact aim; the hit area does not line up with the drawn rafter
findings.detail: Standing next to the rafter the crosshair visibly overlapped it several times while the centre label still said 'Log wall'; it only switched to 'Fallen rafter' after ~2-degree nudges, at a point where the screenshot shows the crosshair slightly off the beam. Debris pick-up has a 12-degree assist, the rafter does not seem to.
findings.repro: after Survey, stand at about (0.8, 0.7) facing yaw ~285; pt look 15 0 repeatedly, reading the centre label each time

findings.title: Four window boards and three floorboards must each be carried to the door one at a time
findings.detail: Each pried board becomes a 'Broken board' to haul. The four window boards took about 140 game seconds of walking (tick 19093 to 23219), across the room four times, with nothing new to do. Picking a board up also needs the view tilted so the board is within ~12 deg of the crosshair; when walkto debris stopped 1.2 m away with the view straight down, E said 'Nothing to pick up there.' Carrying a small armful (or tossing them out through the open window) would cut the dull part.
findings.repro: pry off all 4 window boards; haul them out with e at the board and e by the door

findings.title: Grimy vs clean log walls are nearly indistinguishable, especially from mid-afternoon on
findings.detail: Floor and chimney show progress clearly (swept boards turn lighter and lose their leaf speckle; scrubbed stones turn pale grey). The log walls look uniformly dark brown up close and from a step back, even with the lantern lit (~3:35 pm in game), so you cannot tell which logs are already clean. Only the per-spot centre meter ('Clean here. Move on.' / 'Grimy. Scrub it (2).') tells you, which forces sweeping the crosshair over every log.
findings.repro: after scrubbing a wall corner for ~25 s: pt hold s 1.0; pt shot X; pt key l; pt shot Y

findings.title: Interior too dark to see dirt while sweeping in the Clear step (window still boarded)
findings.detail: Around 1 pm game time the cabin floor is almost black with the window boarded. Sweeping the floor became guesswork: the only signal was 'Clean here. Move on.' on spots already done. Sweeping went at about 10% per 30 game seconds and was the slowest, least readable part of the first 15 minutes. With the lantern on and the crosshair close to the chimney, clean (pale) and sooty (dark) stones were easy to tell apart, and scrubbing went 3x faster. The lantern is only suggested at dusk. Expected: suggest the lantern indoors early, or make the dirty floor readable in the dark.
findings.repro: pt start --profile kindling --game-dir <kindling checkout> --seed 2718; finish Survey; key 1; hold Down to the floor; mousehold while turning; compare with key l (lantern) on

findings.title: No chimney stack or smoke visible outside the cabin once the hearth is lit
findings.detail: With the fire lit and Ada home (Done, about 3:28 pm in game), the cabin seen from the front yard (shots/chim4.png) and from the west side looking toward the hearth wall (this shot) shows a plain roof: no stone chimney stack above it, no smoke, no glow. Inside there is a full stone chimney breast. The 'firelit chimney' payoff of Kindle can't be seen from outside, so the warm cabin looks exactly like the cold one. I did not reach the back (hearth-side) wall itself, but a stack on that gable should rise above the ridge. Expected a chimney through the roof with smoke once the fire takes hold.
findings.repro: pt start (s04 save); finish Kindle; walk out the door; pt hold a 4; pt hold w 4; face the hearth bearing; look at the roof

findings.title: Open roof sections are hard to see from below: the last open section showed only as a thin sliver of sky
findings.detail: Standing under the roof hole looking up, open sections are blue sky and patched ones are grey, but the hole is seen through a deep shaft, so from most spots only part of the opening is visible. After two sections the remaining open area was a strip at the edge of view, and the last one was a 1-2 px blue sliver (roof5.png). The checklist says how many sections are open but not where. All 4 could be found and fixed (aim name 'Hole in the roof' helped), but only by hunting with small look nudges.
findings.repro: stand at about (0.56,-0.08) under the hole with shingles; tilt up to ~60-70 deg; patch sections and look for the remaining blue

findings.title: R while carrying the mantel clock had no visible effect; it always lands facing the room
findings.detail: Picked the placed clock back up, pressed R twice, put it down: it sat the same way on the mantel. Fine if mantel things snap to face out, but nothing says so, while the prompt says 'R to turn'.
findings.repro: place mantel clock (e at the hearth); e to pick it up; r r; e

findings.title: Sweep the floor stalls at ~93%: the last specks in corners are hard to find as the cabin darkens
findings.detail: Floor went 9% -> 89% in about 3 minutes of sweeping, then only 89 -> 93% over two more full passes (ticks 28600-30357). Remaining dirt is in corners, along walls and near the hearth; by 2:30 pm the interior is dim and the dirt speckle is hard to see. Nothing points to where the remaining percent is. The floor line was still not done when I stopped.
findings.repro: sweep the floor with pt key 1 and mousehold while stepping in rows; after ~89% look around with pt hold Up 0.35 and try to spot remaining dirt

findings.title: The mare reads as 'Stall' when aimed at, and walkto mare sticks on the fence
findings.detail: At the stall fence with the crosshair on the mare's body, the label reads 'Stall' with no hint, so you can't tell she can be tended (curry comb 9). The game says she is hungry ('The mare nickers at you, hopefully. She's hungry.'), but nothing visible tells you how to feed her. pt walkto mare stops 2.8 m away, stuck. Expected 'Mare' and a hint when aimed at her.
findings.repro: pt start; after Done, pt walkto mare; pt hold Up 0.4; read the centre label

findings.title: Welcome checklist (Ada's brief) runs to mid-screen and collides with the centre aim label
findings.detail: Once the fire takes hold, the HUD checklist grows to 9 lines (STEP: Welcome plus ADA'S BRIEF). Its last line, 'Something of home on the walls', lands on the centre aim label 'The fire' and covers the top half of the hearth, with two status lines stacked under the crosshair as well. It stays like this through the arrival. Expected the brief to collapse or the HUD to keep the centre clear.
findings.repro: pt start; light the fire while facing the hearth; take a shot as the fire takes hold

findings.title: Woodpile beside the hearth needs a near-exact aim; E with a split log at the hearth does nothing
findings.detail: While carrying a split log, pressing E with the crosshair on the hearth, the chimney or the floor next to the rack only repeats 'Stack it on the woodpile by the hearth, or lay it in the hearth (E)'. The woodpile is a thin rack of posts tucked against the chimney's left side, and its 2 stacked logs are tiny stubs that barely show. The label 'Woodpile (2 logs)' appears only across a few degrees of yaw, and it reads 'not in reach' unless you stand right over it in the corner. Stacking one log took about 4 real minutes of hunting (ticks 9534 to 14086). Expected E with a log near the hearth to snap to the woodpile, the way debris gets about 12 degrees of forgiveness, and the stacked logs to be clearly visible.
findings.repro: pt start (save carries a split log); pt walkto hearth; pt key e (nothing); try aiming at the rack left of the chimney

findings.title: Build in the 0.2.0 run reports version 0.1.2
findings.detail: state.json and session.json both say version 0.1.2 (commit 7ecf1fe) though this is the 0.2.0 playtest run. The save itself loaded fine with 'Loaded your save.'
findings.repro: pt start ...; pt state --full | grep version
alsoTitled: Build reports version 0.1.2 in the 0.2.0 playtest

findings.title: Checklist HUD text has no backing, so it is hard to read over pale surfaces
findings.detail: The checklist in the top left (white/grey text, no shadow panel) is nearly unreadable over the freshly scrubbed pale chimney stones ('Scrub the walls (13%)'), and it was also hard to read over the snow drift. A dark outline or a translucent panel would fix it.
findings.repro: scrub the chimney (key 2, mousehold) until the stones are pale, then look at them from close range
alsoTitled: Light checklist text is hard to read over the pale chimney stones

findings.title: Aim label 'The fire' is drawn over the flames
findings.detail: Looking at the lit hearth, the label 'The fire' sits right on top of the flames and hides the fire the player has just lit (also in shots/f1.png). Expected the label below the crosshair, or faded once the fire is lit.
findings.repro: pt start; light the fire; face the hearth at about -20 pitch

findings.title: Clear-step percentages on screen differ from actual cleanliness without saying so
findings.detail: 'Sweep the floor (53%)' was shown while the probe had floorClean 0.45, and the chimney showed 78% at hearthClean 0.59. The HUD shows progress toward a hidden threshold. That is fine, but a new player cannot tell how much is left, and the starting 9-13% suggests the area is already partly clean. The build also reports version 0.1.2 in a run labelled 0.2.0 (worth checking).
findings.repro: compare pt state checklist text with progress.floorClean / hearthClean

findings.title: Debris counter goes UP from 15 to 17 after sawing the rafter
findings.detail: 'Haul out the debris (15 left)' became '(17 left)' once the rafter was sawn into three lengths. A status line explains it ('Sawn into three lengths... three pieces to haul out instead of one'), so it is understandable, but a progress counter going backwards right after finishing a job feels like a setback and the message is easy to miss at low fps. Consider counting the rafter as 3 from the start.
findings.repro: pt key 4; aim at the fallen rafter; pt mousehold 10 (repeat until sawn); read checklist line 1

findings.title: Long checklist lines drop to a smaller font than the rest
findings.detail: 'Replace the rotten floorboards (3 left)' in Repair and 'No dark corners: a candle, and curtains' / 'Somewhere to sit and sew, with a quilt to hand' in Furnish render noticeably smaller than their neighbours, so the list looks uneven.
findings.repro: load the save; look at the checklist; finish Repair and look again

findings.title: Releasing the match silently resets its progress to 0%
findings.detail: Holding the match to the kindling for 2 s and then 4 s gave 35% and 70%, but between holds 'The match goes out' and the meter went back to 0%. At 3-4 fps it took one unbroken hold of about 10 s to catch. The message is clear, but the cost of letting go is steep with nothing to warn you. Polish only.
findings.repro: pt key 8; pt mousehold 2; pt mousehold 4; read the meter; pt mousehold 10

findings.title: Restoration playback ends with the player avatar blocking the lit fire and Ada hidden by the quilt
findings.detail: The reveal and the T playback end on the finished, firelit cabin, but the player's own figure stands on the rug directly in front of the hearth and hides the new fire. Ada in the chair shows only as a purple skirt because the quilt hides her upper body. This is the game's payoff shot. Expected the final frame to leave the hearth and Ada clear, for example by hiding the avatar or moving the camera. See shots/replay_grid.png (frames from the T playback) and shots/reveal_grid.png (the automatic reveal).
findings.repro: pt start; finish Kindle and Welcome; pt key t; screenshot every 2-3 s

findings.title: Roof hole survey check needs the crosshair right on the open sky patch
findings.detail: Standing under the hole and looking up with the opening clearly on screen (off-centre by ~20 degrees), the label stayed 'Ceiling boards' and the checklist did not tick; it ticked only once the crosshair was on the blue gap.
findings.repro: after the other survey items: walk to about (0.8, 0.7), pt hold Up 1.2, look around the hole

findings.title: Survey checklist line 'Hole in the roof (stand under it, look up)' is drawn in a smaller font
findings.detail: That one checklist item is visibly shrunk compared with the others, apparently to fit. The parenthetical instruction is genuinely helpful, but the mismatched size looks like a bug.
findings.repro: pt start ...; pt shot
